observation.visible_scene: A single leafless tree silhouetted on a dark, flat horizon line, set against a star-filled night sky that brightens toward a pale glow just above the horizon. Below the horizon a calm body of water mirrors the scene: the sky's gradient and an inverted reflection of the tree hang directly beneath the real tree, symmetric about the horizon. The tree and its reflection occupy the center of the frame throughout.
visible_changes: The tree silhouette, the horizon line, and the tree's reflection keep the same position and shape from the first to the last sampled frame; no translation, scaling, or deformation of these elements is discernible.

Small bright specks/highlights on the water surface appear, fade, and shift position between frames (e.g., isolated dots on the right and left of the reflective band), indicating minor, localized changes in the water's surface or drifting particles rather than movement of the tree or reflection.
The overall sky gradient and star field look essentially unchanged frame to frame; no obvious drift or rotation of the stars is detectable at this sampling rate.
The framing of the horizon and tree relative to the image edges stays fixed, so no camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the surface specks and any faint shimmer (wind, particles, reflections of meteors, sensor noise) is not shown.
Whether the scene is a still frame, a slow timelapse, or a real-time shot cannot be determined from this short excerpt.
Any motion of the stars or water outside the sampled interval is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether the bright dots on the water are true moving objects or transient glints/noise is ambiguous.
Any extremely slow drift of the star field or subtle ripple distortion of the reflection is below reliable detection in these frames.
Camera motion cannot be fully ruled out given the static background, but no relative change supports it.
